the distribution of Mg2+ is significantly different in MHS muscles, and that the distribution of calcium is not different in MHS and normal muscles.
Ca2+ and, in particular, Mg2+ content of skeletal muscle are different in malignant hyperthermia-susceptible subjects.

MHS muscle contains a greater population of muscle fibres with higher Mg2+ content.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ and/or Mg2+ content may be a useful tool in the diagnosis of MHS.
MHS muscle is not different in its Ca2+ content compared to normal muscle, whereas the distribution of Mg2+ is different and may contribute to a greater Mg2+ content in MHS muscle.
the Ca2+ and/or Mg2+ contents of skeletal muscle are not the sole determinants of malignant hyperthermia susceptibility.
